The board is ratifying (approving after the fact) the agreement, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Street Academy Foundation up to $736,835 to run Street Academy, an alternative high school
output.summary: Street Academy Foundation will operate the Emiliano Zapata Street Academy, an alternative high school for credit recovery and dropout prevention. It serves about 115 at-risk students in grades 9-12 using an independent study model. The agreement runs from August 7, 2023 to May 23, 2024 and began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Agency for Children up to $60,000 for a bilingual mental health provider at Greenleaf
output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children will provide a Spanish-speaking mental health provider at Greenleaf Elementary School. The provider will counsel 10-15 children one on one each week on well-being, social skills and trauma. The agreement runs from August 7, 2023 to May 31, 2024 and began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Blueprint Schools Network up to $70,000 for small-group math tutoring for middle school students
output.summary: Blueprint Schools Network will provide small-group math tutoring during the regular school day for middle school students. This includes supporting a full-time Math Fellow who can cover for absent tutors or add help at a campus. The agreement runs from September 27, 2023 to June 30, 2024 and began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Northeastern University's Mills campus up to $39,420 for teacher inquiry work on social emotional learning

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $39,420.00

output.summary: Northeastern University-Mills College Campus (Lead by Learning) will work with elementary social emotional learning lead teachers on a districtwide teacher inquiry partnership. The goal is to build teachers' skills by looking closely at students' daily learning. The service period began August 1, 2023, before the Board's October vote to ratify it, and runs through June 28, 2024.

vendor.name: Northeastern University-Mills College Campus, Lead by Learning

output.headline: Pays Children Rising up to $5,000 for an early math program at Sankofa United Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: Children Rising will run its Path2Mth early numeracy program at Sankofa United Elementary School. It gives foundational math help to students who are performing well below grade level. The service period began September 25, 2023, before the Board's vote to ratify it, and runs through May 15, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Children Rising up to $5,000 for one-on-one reading tutoring at Sankofa United Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: Children Rising will provide its Succeeding by Reading early literacy program at Sankofa United Elementary School. Students referred by school staff who lack foundational reading skills get weekly one-on-one tutoring. The service period began October 9, 2023, before the Board's vote to ratify it, and runs through May 15, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Playworks up to $59,000 for a school-culture coach at Acorn Woodland Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $59,000.00

output.summary: Playworks will provide a fully trained coach at Acorn Woodland Elementary School. The coach uses games, strategies and systems to build a positive school culture. The service period began August 7, 2023, before the Board's vote to ratify it, and runs through May 24, 2024.

output.headline: Approves no-cost U.S. Geological Survey work-based learning program for students with disabilities
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (a formal partnership agreement) with the U.S. Geological Survey brings its STEP-UP work-based learning experiences to students with disabilities, mostly ages 18 to 22. The goal is to build job readiness and independent living skills. It runs from September 29, 2023 through September 29, 2026 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $105,000 for media academy supports at Oakland International High

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $105,000.00

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title says 2023-2024 but the stated service period runs from September 1, 2023 through May 30, 2025.
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will provide classroom academic supports and mentors for expanded learning in the media academy at Oakland International High School. The service period is September 1, 2023 through May 30, 2025. The title calls this a 2023-2024 agreement, but the stated period runs into the 2024-25 school year.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $56,000 for two AmeriCorps Fellows on school waste prevention
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources provides two AmeriCorps Fellows to support schools and the district on waste prevention programs, including building and maintaining the physical and social systems that make them work. The agreement is through the Custodial Services Department and runs from September 11, 2023 to July 31, 2024. The agreement period began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $200,000 for The Genesis Group to provide special education services

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $200,000.00

output.summary: The Genesis Group is a nonpublic agency (outside the district) that will provide special education services required by students' Individualized Education Programs. This is a master contract for July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, run through the Special Education Department. The amount is a cap, not a guaranteed payment.

output.headline: Pays Luna Dance Institute up to $20,000 to train early childhood teachers in using dance

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00

output.summary: Luna Dance Institute will continue building the skills of the district's early childhood education teachers to use dance as a culturally responsive teaching strategy. The work is meant to be sustained through peer leadership and support. The service period began October 2, 2023, before the Board's vote to ratify it, and runs through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Melissa Early Education LLC up to $55,325 for anti-bias practice work with early childhood staff

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $55,325.00

output.summary: Melissa Early Education LLC will continue working with the Early Childhood Development Department's educators and leaders to build anti-bias, anti-hate and anti-racist practices, as described in an exhibit to the agreement. The service period began September 25, 2023, before the Board's vote to ratify it, and runs through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Exzachly Ventures LLC up to $5,000 to assess facility needs at early learning sites

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: Exzachly Ventures LLC will act as a consultant to analyze the current condition of facilities at all of the district's early learning sites. It will also develop a system for prioritizing facility improvements, using an individual with real estate and early childhood expertise. The service period began October 2, 2023, before the Board's vote to ratify it, and runs through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts a $150,000 Zellerbach Family Foundation grant for wellness and belonging at Oakland International High
output.summary: The district accepts $150,000 from the Zellerbach Family Foundation to support Oakland International High School's Wellness, Equity & Belonging Project. The grant period runs from June 1, 2023 through May 31, 2026, and began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a student data-sharing agreement with CORE Districts for research projects through June 2024
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title names Teaching Strategies, LLC, but the action text describes an agreement with CORE Districts.
output.summary: This data sharing agreement lets the district send student data to CORE Districts for the PACE/CORE Research Collaborative and the High School Breakthrough Success Collaborative. It also covers how CORE Districts must protect that data. The agreement period began July 1, 2021, well before this vote, and runs through June 30, 2024. No cost is stated.

output.headline: Accepts $225,000 from the City of Oakland to pay stipends for students in summer internships
output.summary: This first amendment to a grant agreement with the City of Oakland accepts $225,000 in Oakland Fund for Children and Youth money for support stipends for students in summer internships. The internships are part of a high school career pathway program (Exploring College, Career, and Community Options) at 13 high school sites. The agreement period runs June 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024. The text does not say what the amendment changes beyond this.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the October 11, 2023 regular Board meeting
output.summary: The Board ratifies the written minutes of its regular meeting on October 11, 2023. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Approves a labor agreement with the Building and Construction Trades Council for skilled trade workers through 2026
output.summary: The Board approves a tentative agreement with the Building and Construction Trades Council of Alameda County, which represents the district's skilled trade workers such as carpenters, electricians, painters and plumbers. It covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2026, and all other terms of the prior agreement stay in effect. The text does not state a dollar cost.

output.headline: Ratifies the Board President's appointment of a first-term member to the Measure G1 oversight commission
output.summary: The Board ratifies the Board President's appointment of Christian Martinez, in a first term, to the Measure G1 Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission. The appointment takes effect October 26, 2023 and fills an unexpired term ending April 15, 2024.
